note: Bavli: [Kiddushin 32b:4](sefaria:Kiddushin.32b.4) (4 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabban Gamliel”. Beribi after Rabban Gamliel (II), said by R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua. Also Shabbat 115a:7. Footnote 148 has no Rabban + Beribi example.
Bavli: [Arakhin 16b:7](sefaria:Arakhin.16b.7) (1 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel”. Steinsaltz: 'Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Great'. Beribi replaces the patronymic.

Bavli: [Sukkah 26a:7](sefaria:Sukkah.26a.7) (3 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabbi Yosei the Great”. Also AZ 8b:19 'רבי יוסי ברבי' (Steinsaltz: R. Yosei the Great = R. Yosei b. Halafta). Count excludes 'ברבי + father's name'.
Bavli: [Menachot 34b:6](sefaria:Menachot.34b.6) (1 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabbi Yehuda the Distinguished”. Steinsaltz: 'Rabbi Yehuda the Distinguished [Beribbi]'.

Bavli: [Makkot 5b:10](sefaria:Makkot.5b.10) (5 segments). Gazetteer: “the Distinguished One”. Beribi used alone as the name of a tanna ('his father said to him'). Also Chullin 52b:15, 52b:18; Chullin 57a:6, 137a:21.

Bavli: [Bava Batra 51b:5](sefaria:Bava_Batra.51b.5) (1 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabban Ukva and Rabban Neḥemya, the sons of Rav’s daughters”. Rabban for Babylonian grandsons of Rav, not the Nasi house. Same pair called 'רבנא עוקבא ורבנא נחמיה' at Chullin 92a:5. Paper footnote 149 says Rabban was for the Nasi.

Bavli: [Beitzah 29a:15](sefaria:Beitzah.29a.15) (4 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabbana Ukva the orphan”. Rabbana + given name. Also 'רבנא עוקבא יתמא' Gittin 52a:19. The paper gives no Rabbana example (footnote 152 cites only Ornstein).
Bavli: [Shabbat 20b:9](sefaria:Shabbat.20b.9) (2 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabbana Neḥemya, brother of the Exilarch”. 'רבנא נחמיה אחוה דריש גלותא'. Rabbana for a member of the Exilarch's family.

Bavli: [Sanhedrin 30a:5](sefaria:Sanhedrin.30a.5) (3 segments). Gazetteer: “Rabbana Ashi”. In a quoted court-document formula ('ואמר לן רבנא אשי'); also Ketubot 22a:4. Shows Rabbana as a title for Rav Ashi in documents.

Bavli: [Avodah Zarah 5b:2](sefaria:Avodah_Zarah.5b.2) (77 segments). Gazetteer: “Moses our teacher”. Honorific suffix ‘our teacher’: משה רבינו (77 segments) and רבינו הקדוש for Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi (6, e.g. Pesachim 37a:4). Not in the paper in any form.
